component.name: Windup
component.summary: Clipboard history and plain-text paste behind a hotkey

description.p: Press Super+V and a popup opens at your cursor with everything you have copied, images included. Pick an entry and Windup pastes it into the window you were in. Super+Shift+V pastes what is on the clipboard with its formatting stripped.

It works on Wayland and on X11. On COSMIC, KDE Plasma, Sway, Hyprland and other wlroots desktops it watches the clipboard and pastes through the compositor's own protocols; on GNOME it asks once for permission to paste. Copies a password manager marks as secret are never recorded.
Recordings with sound play in every player, and the capture bar keeps its Area, Window and Full screen choice after a selection; dragging outside the selection draws a new one.

Screen recording: an area, a window or the whole screen to MP4, WebM, MOV, MKV or GIF, with optional computer sound and microphone, a recording bar that stays out of the video, and a Video settings pane.
After an update, the running Windup hands over to the new version by itself instead of answering the shortcuts until it is stopped.
Print Screen opens the capture bar and Ctrl+Shift+S takes a screenshot; Print Screen, Scroll Lock and Pause can be chosen for any shortcut; redo is Ctrl+Y.
Screenshots: a capture bar over a frozen screen for an area, a window or a whole screen, an editor to draw, blur and mosaic, and copy or save. The shortcuts set in the settings window are used now.
The clipboard history opens at the pointer on COSMIC, the list shows when each entry was copied, and settings show the version with a link to the source.
Binds Super+V by itself on COSMIC, and the screen no longer turns black when the clipboard history opens.
First release: clipboard history and plain-text paste, on Windows and Linux.
